ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, take the hypotenuse $BC$ of the right triangle $\triangle ABC$ as a side to construct a square $BCEF$ on the same side of $\triangle ABC$. Let the center of the square be $O$, and connect $AO$. If $AB=2$ and $AO=3\sqrt{2}$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw line OD $\perp$ OA, intersecting AC at D, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral BCEF is a square, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BOC=90$^\circ$, OB=OC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOB+$\angle$BOD=90$^\circ$, $\angle$DOC+$\angle$BOD=90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOB=$\angle$DOC, \\
$\because$ $\angle$ODC=$\angle$OAC+$\angle$AOD, $\angle$OAB=$\angle$OAC+$\angle$BAC, $\angle$AOD=$\angle$BAC=90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAB=$\angle$ODC, \\
In $\triangle$ABO and $\triangle$DCO, $ \{\begin{array}{l}\angle OAB=\angle ODC\hfill \\ \angle AOB=\angle DOC\hfill \\ OB=OC\hfill \end{array}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ABO$\cong$$\triangle$DCO, \\
$\therefore$ OA=OD= $3\sqrt{2}$, CD=AB=2, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$OAD is an isosceles right triangle, \\
$\therefore$ AD= $ \sqrt{2}OA$ =6, \\
$\therefore$ AC=AD+CD=\boxed{8}.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/vector route: From the figure and text, model the right triangle with A as the origin, AB along one coordinate axis and AC along the other. Let B=(2,0), C=(0,x), where x=AC. Then BC has length s=√(x²+4) and midpoint M=(1,x/2). Since the square is constructed on BC on the same side as A, the center O is obtained by moving from M by s/2 in the unit normal direction toward A. For vector BC=(-2,x), that unit normal is (-x,-2)/s, so O=M+(s/2)(-x,-2)/s=(1-x/2, x/2-1). Therefore AO²=(1-x/2)²+(x/2-1)²=(x-2)²/2. Given AO=3√2, get (x-2)²/2=18, so |x-2|=6. Since x is a positive length, x=8. Hence AC=8.

推理：按坐标法建模。令 A 为原点，AB 沿 x 轴，AC 沿 y 轴。因为 AB=2，设 B=(2,0)，C=(0,x)，其中 x=AC。则 BC 的中点为 M=(1,x/2)，向量 BC=C-B=(-2,x)，长度 s=√(x²+4)。正方形 BCEF 与三角形 ABC 在 BC 的同侧，所以正方形中心 O 是从 M 沿指向 A 所在一侧的法向量移动 s/2 得到。向量 BC 的该侧单位法向量为 (-x,-2)/s，因此 O=M+(s/2)·((-x,-2)/s)=(1-x/2, x/2-1)。

因为 A=(0,0)，所以 AO²=(1-x/2)²+(x/2-1)²=2(1-x/2)²=(x-2)²/2。已知 AO=3√2，所以 AO²=18，即 (x-2)²/2=18，得到 (x-2)²=36，因此 |x-2|=6。由于 x=AC 是正长度，x=8。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, take the hypotenuse $BC$ of the right triangle $\triangle ABC$ as a side to construct a square $BCEF$ on the same side of $\triangle ABC$. Let the center of the square be $O$, and connect $AO$. If $AB=2$ and $AO=3\sqrt{2}$, what is the length of $AC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw line OD $\perp$ OA, intersecting AC at D, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral BCEF is a square, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BOC=90$^\circ$, OB=OC, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOB+$\angle$BOD=90$^\circ$, $\angle$DOC+$\angle$BOD=90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$AOB=$\angle$DOC, \\
$\because$ $\angle$ODC=$\angle$OAC+$\angle$AOD, $\angle$OAB=$\angle$OAC+$\angle$BAC, $\angle$AOD=$\angle$BAC=90$^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OAB=$\angle$ODC, \\
In $\triangle$ABO and $\triangle$DCO, $ \{\begin{array}{l}\angle OAB=\angle ODC\hfill \\ \angle AOB=\angle DOC\hfill \\ OB=OC\hfill \end{array}$, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ABO$\cong$$\triangle$DCO, \\
$\therefore$ OA=OD= $3\sqrt{2}$, CD=AB=2, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$OAD is an isosceles right triangle, \\
$\therefore$ AD= $ \sqrt{2}OA$ =6, \\
$\therefore$ AC=AD+CD=\boxed{8}
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure there is a square BCEF, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, E is at the upper right, and F is at the upper left; the two diagonals of the square intersect at the center O. Point A is located on the left side near B, and line segments AB and AC form right triangle ABC; the figure marks a right angle at A, and AO has been connected.
Then reason: According to the specified method, through O draw OD⊥AO, intersecting AC at D. Because BCEF is a square and O is the center of the square, OB=OC, and ∠BOC=90°. Also because OD⊥AO, ∠AOD=90°. Thus ∠AOB+∠BOD=90°, and at the same time ∠DOC+∠BOD=90°, therefore ∠AOB=∠DOC. Also because ∠BAC=90° and ∠AOD=90°, and D is on AC, through angle relationships it can be obtained that ∠OAB=∠ODC. Thus, in △ABO and △DCO, there are ∠OAB=∠ODC, ∠AOB=∠DOC, OB=OC, so △ABO≅△DCO. Therefore CD=AB=2, OD=OA=3√2. Since OD⊥OA and OD=OA, △AOD is an isosceles right triangle, AD=OA·√2=3√2·√2=6. Finally AC=AD+CD=6+2=8.
